diagnosis: All four rollouts revealed all four decisive facts (PF1-PF4) and cited them in justification_fact_ids, so the failures are ENCODING MISMATCH problems, not disclosure or telepathy problems. C4 (gated by PF3, the 07:00-07:15 monitoring window) failed in 4/4 rollouts even though A4 consistently revealed that exact time range and the settlements encoded it (e.g., 'Elena will check transmitted readings daily 07:00-07:15' in the onboarding_scheduling commitment). C2 (gated by PF2, the 'Bluetooth blood-pressure cuff with twice-daily readings' and 'Bluetooth scale with daily readings' device strings) failed in 1/4 rollouts (rollout 3) where the settlement split the device names and frequencies into separate fields/commitments instead of matching the expected combined string format. C3 (also gated by PF3, the Tuesday 15:30 onboarding time) failed in 1/4 rollouts (rollout 0) despite the settlement containing 'Tuesday 15:30 next week' as onboarding_datetime — suggesting the check rejects the 'next week' suffix or expects a different field. The core problem is that check thresholds for C2 and C4 are too rigidly worded to match the natural encodings models produce even when the underlying information is correctly surfaced and cited.
